label: Late original-phase / delimiter input of i, j, u, b, t or <DEL> (very sparse, context-dependent)
explanation: Fires only in the original phase and on the delimiter step, never during copying. Activity concentrates in the last 1-2 original positions and on <DEL>, mostly for long sequences (L=8-9). Firing rate peaks at orig_idx 8 with 19x lift. Input tokens are mostly i, j, u, b, t or <DEL>, and usually the first occurrence of that token. Preceding tokens 0, l, y, a raise the rate. The predicate (t>=6, original/delimiter phase, input in {i,j,u,b,t,<DEL>}) covers about 77% of activation mass, but precision is only about 0.4%: the feature fires on roughly 1 in 250 such steps. The extra conditions tried (previous token, earlier tokens such as y/0/k, to_go) raise precision to at most about 3%, at a large cost in recall. Whatever decides firing within this context is not captured by simple token-history variables. Magnitude is weak (mean 0.13, max 0.27) and is not clearly tied to any variable checked. It does not fire at t<3 or anywhere in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=0 (+3.96), orig0=3 (+3.09), prev_tok=l (+3.08), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=u (+2.99), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=j (+2.98), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=b (+2.52). Lower it: phase=2 (-5.57), prev3_tok=- (-4.17), orig1=0 (-3.51), next_out=- (-1.44).
